newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T., Imperial up on fund decision.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T., Imperial up on fund decision.

text.p: Shares in British tobacco companies B.A.T. Industries and Imperial Tobacco rose on Tuesday as investors took heart from news a major U.S investment fund rejected a resolution to divest its tobacco holdings.
B.A.T was up eight pence at 428p, with 1.47 million shares traded, and Imperial was up 5-1/2p at 364p with just over half a million shares changing hands.
On Monday, Philip Morris Cos Inc shares rallied after College Retirement Equities Fund participants rejected a resolution which had urged divesting any holdings related to the tobacco industry.
"That has helped sentiment in the sector," one marketmaker said in London.

Analysts said the U.S. fund decision reflected hopes that, with the U.S. election over, attacks on the industry might subside. They said the Clinton administration and the tobacco industry might work out some form of compromise.
Marketmakers noted also that pressure from futures-selling had abated in recent days in London and the overall market was rising gently. By 1002 GMT the FTSE 100 share index was up 0.45 percent.
